_about: Editorial notes for /audit, keyed by benchmark name and merged into the generated table by render_audit.py. Numbers NEVER live here — they come from nulltest_audit_results.json. This file exists so that regenerating the page cannot silently delete a published correction, and so that editing prose cannot silently change a measurement. render_audit.py reports any note whose benchmark has left the table rather than dropping it.
bielik-entity-familiarity-v2: CORRECTED 2026-07-26: worst-cell A* was published as 0.742 and is actually 0.953. Every cell in this row is tied at the permutation floor, and a tie-break bug in our own tool resolved ties by iteration order instead of effect size, so the LAST null in order won and the reported figure was the mildest of the tied cells, not the worst. The verdict was never affected. We UNDERSTATED how strongly this corpus separates.

geometry-of-truth/sp_en_trans: n=354 is INSIDE the region where a known-contaminated corpus also passes (<600 on the measured curve) — read this verdict with that in mind.
aperture/verifydomain-claims-147: RESTORED 2026-07-27: this row was absent from the served table for weeks. It is the battery behind the retracted front-page headline, and it is the worst artifact we have produced. It was missing not because it was hidden but because the results file was never regenerated after the manifest grew — which is the same thing from the reader's side.
aperture/knowledge-prominence-v1: ADDED 2026-07-27: served and cited on /calibrate, but never in this manifest — so the claim above to cover "every one of our own" was false for as long as that page has been live.
aperture/knowledge-prominence-v2: ADDED 2026-07-27: served but cited on no page. In the table so that being unpublished is not a way to stay unaudited.
aperture/prominence-people-v1: CHANGED 2026-10-24 (nulltest v1.3): PASS under the four probes of v1.2, DISQUALIFIED now. The surname's initial letter recovers the labels at A* 0.661 because the builder sampled the alphabetically-first 200 members of each Wikipedia category. v1.3 added two alphabet-position probes for that class of construction artifact. The probe was written after the miss; this row is why.
aperture/grounding-coordinate: CORRECTED 2026-10-24 (nulltest v1.4), the same day: DISQUALIFIED under v1.2 (worst cell length/eponymous_signs, A* 0.855, n=28, adjusted p 0.030 over 18 cells); PASS under v1.3 for part of a day (same cell, adjusted p 0.057 over 35 cells); DISQUALIFIED under v1.4 (same cell, same A*, adjusted p 0.037 over the same 35 cells), marked BORDERLINE. v1.3's permutation null shuffled labels across strata and its family-wise correction was biased at the permutation floor; both are fixed in v1.4 and the PASS did not survive the fix. The battery never changed. A verdict this close to the line is reported as borderline in either direction.
truthfulqa/answers: ADDED 2026-10-24 with nulltest 1.3; RE-SCORED under v1.4 the same day. The verdict is unchanged. The worst cell is now words/Law (n=586, A* 0.857) rather than a small category at A* 1.000: ties at the permutation floor are now broken by effect size, and the permutation count was raised to 8,900 so that 222 cells can be resolved at alpha 0.05. 63 of 222 cells separate (77 under v1.3's biased correction). The finding is corpus-wide. The `words` probe's feature table (run `python3 nulltest.py TruthfulQA.csv --explode "Correct Answers=0,Incorrect Answers=1" --split ";" --stratum-key Category --explain`) shows the artifact: the correct-answer column carries hedges the incorrect column almost never does ("I have no comment" appears in 86 correct answers and 0 incorrect; "do not" in 83 against 4). A model that learned to hedge scores on TruthfulQA without knowing anything; this is a known criticism of the benchmark and the table now measures it.
halueval/qa: ADDED 2026-10-24 with nulltest 1.3. The hallucinated answers were written by ChatGPT and the right answers are HotpotQA's short reference strings, so the two classes differ in length and register before any question is read. The row says how much: see its A*. A judge model scored on HaluEval QA by answer alone can earn that much of its score from form.
halueval/dialogue: ADDED 2026-10-24 with nulltest 1.3. Same construction as halueval/qa: a human reference response against a ChatGPT-written hallucinated one, scored without the dialogue they answer. The row says how far apart the two registers sit; see its A* and the WHY tables from `--explain`.
truth-is-universal/facts: RE-SCORED 2026-10-24 under nulltest v1.4: DISQUALIFIED as before, now marked BORDERLINE (adjusted p 0.038, within a factor of two of the line). A single `length` cell carries it.
aperture/calibration-battery-v1: RE-SCORED 2026-10-24 under nulltest v1.4: 15 of 34 cells separate (17 under v1.3, 16 of 18 under v1.2); worst cell unchanged at A* 1.000.
_corrections_2026-10-24: Every row was re-scored under nulltest v1.4 on 2026-10-24 after a statistics review found that v1.3's null was not stratified and its family-wise correction was biased at the permutation floor. 16 of 17 verdicts are unchanged; aperture/grounding-coordinate changed. Adjusted p values across the table moved off the old floor (0.0017) because the correction now p-values observed and permuted statistics from the same pool.
